findings.name: 100% Disabled Veteran Property Tax Exemption
findings.description: New Jersey provides a full annual property tax exemption on the principal residence of an honorably discharged veteran who was 100% permanently and totally disabled during active duty service, per VA certification. The exemption also extends to the surviving spouse/civil union/domestic partner of such a veteran (or of a veteran who died on active duty), provided the surviving spouse has not remarried or entered a new civil union/domestic partnership, was a legal NJ resident, and the deceased veteran was an NJ resident at death. Applicants file Form D.V.S.S.E. with the local assessor, along with proof documents (DD-214, VA disability certification, deed, and for surviving spouses, death certificate and marriage/civil union certificate). Denials may be appealed via Form A-1 to the County Board of Taxation by April 1 (January 15 in Burlington, Gloucester, and Monmouth counties).
findings.value: Full exemption from property tax on principal residence
otherReqs: Honorable discharge from active duty service
VA certification of 100% permanent and total service-connected disability
Must own and occupy the dwelling as principal residence
Surviving spouse must not have remarried or entered a new civil union/domestic partnership
findings.agency: NJ Division of Taxation / Local Municipal Assessor
findings.form: D.V.S.S.E. (Claim for Property Tax Exemption on Dwelling of Disabled Veteran or Surviving Spouse)
documentation: VA certification of 100% permanent and total service-connected disability
findings.sourceExcerpt: If you are an honorably discharged veteran who was 100% permanently and totally disabled during active duty service, you may qualify for an annual property tax exemption on your principal or primary residence. You must provide a U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs certification of active duty service-connected disability stating you are 100% permanently and totally disabled.

findings.name: Free Vehicle Registration for Blind or Adaptive-Vehicle Disabled Veterans
findings.description: New Jersey waives vehicle registration fees for veterans who are blind due to war service, or who received a free automobile from the VA through the VA automobile grant, provided the vehicle is equipped with special adaptive attachments or devices necessary for its safe operation and is insured by a NJ-licensed insurer. This is narrower than the standard Disabled Veteran license plate, which itself carries a $15 fee. Applications require VA certification and are mailed to the NJ Motor Vehicle Commission.
findings.value: Free vehicle registration for qualifying blind/VA-automobile-grant veterans
otherReqs: Blind due to war service, OR received a VA automobile grant with adaptive equipment installed
Vehicle must be insured by a NJ-licensed insurance company
Standard Disabled Veteran license plate costs $15 and does not itself waive registration fees
documentation: VA certification of blindness or automobile grant
findings.sourceExcerpt: Eligibility includes veterans who are blind due to war service or those with service-connected disabilities who received a free automobile from the VA. The vehicle in question is equipped with special attachments or devices that may be necessary for its safe operation. Applications require VA certification and should be mailed to the NJ Motor Vehicle Commission.

findings.name: Disabled Veteran Free Hunting & Fishing License
findings.description: Honorably discharged New Jersey resident veterans of any branch of the Armed Forces with a VA-recognized service-connected disability of any degree qualify for free hunting and fishing licenses, permits, and stamps with no transaction fee at license agents (a small shipping/handling fee applies for online orders). Veterans must first be certified by NJ Fish & Wildlife by mailing VA proof of disability, discharge documentation, and residency proof to the Trenton office (certification cannot be completed online or at an agent). Certified disabled veterans also receive two free spring turkey permits and one free fall turkey permit annually, plus additional free permits during leftover sales, though they receive no preferential treatment in permit lotteries.
findings.value: Free hunting/fishing licenses, permits, and stamps; free spring/fall turkey permits
otherReqs: Any degree of VA-recognized service-connected disability qualifies
Initial certification must be done by mail to the Trenton Fish & Wildlife office (not online or in-agent)
No preferential treatment in permit lotteries
findings.agency: New Jersey Division of Fish and Wildlife
documentation: VA proof of service-connected disability (certification letter or wallet card)
DD-214 or equivalent honorable discharge documentation
findings.sourceExcerpt: Honorably discharged resident veterans of any branch of the Armed Forces of the United States declared by the US Department of Veteran Affairs to have a service-connected disability of any degree qualify for free hunting and fishing licenses, permits and stamps. Certified disabled veterans receive two complimentary spring turkey permits annually and one free fall turkey permit yearly.

findings.name: Veterans' Tuition Credit Program
findings.description: New Jersey's Veterans' Tuition Credit Program (N.J.S.A. 18A:71-64 et seq.) reimburses approved NJ educational institutions to offset the cost of tuition for eligible Vietnam-era veterans. To qualify, the veteran must have served on active duty between December 31, 1960 and May 7, 1975, and been a legal NJ resident at the time of entrance into or discharge from service, or for the two years immediately preceding application. Maximum reimbursement is $400 per year for full-time students and $200 per year for part-time students.
findings.value: Up to $400/year (full-time) or $200/year (part-time) tuition reimbursement to the institution
otherReqs: Active duty service between December 31, 1960 and May 7, 1975
NJ legal residency at entrance/discharge, or for 2 years immediately preceding application
Must attend an approved NJ educational institution
findings.agency: NJ Department of Military and Veterans Affairs, Veterans Benefits Bureau
findings.form: Application for Veterans Tuition Credit Program
findings.sourceExcerpt: Veterans attending any approved educational institution may apply for the Veterans Tuition Credit Program, under which partial reimbursement is provided to the institution to offset the cost of the veteran's tuition. To qualify, the veteran must have been on active duty between Dec. 31, 1960, and May 7, 1975, and have been a legal resident of NJ at the time of entrance into or discharge from the service. Maximum reimbursement is $400 per year for full-time students, $200 for part-time students.

findings.name: Civil Service Absolute Veterans Preference
findings.description: New Jersey grants an "absolute veterans preference" on Civil Service Commission examinations: qualified veterans who receive a passing score are placed at the top of an open competitive employment list ahead of non-veterans, regardless of numeric score, and eligible disabled veterans receive the highest preference, ranked above both veterans and non-veterans. Under the "Rule of Three," an appointing authority may select any of the top three ranked candidates unless a veteran appears among them. Preference extends to the spouse of a disabled veteran (if not already employed in a civil service position) and to the surviving spouse of a disabled veteran or of any veteran who died in service, until remarriage. Eligibility requires an honorable discharge from active duty during a qualifying war era per P.L. 2007, c.115, and applicants must complete a Civil Service Veterans Preference Claim Form through the NJ Department of Veterans Affairs.
findings.value: Absolute preference placing qualified veterans atop open competitive employment lists; disabled veterans ranked highest
otherReqs: Honorable discharge with qualifying war-era service dates per P.L. 2007, c.115
Preference can be established as late as 8 days before an open competitive employment list is issued
Spousal/surviving-spouse preference has its own conditions (non-employment in civil service; no remarriage)
findings.agency: NJ Civil Service Commission / NJ Department of Veterans Affairs
findings.form: Civil Service Veterans Preference Claim Form
documentation: DD-214 showing qualifying war-era service and honorable discharge
findings.sourceExcerpt: New Jersey grants absolute veterans preference meaning that qualified veterans are placed at the top of an open competitive employment list ahead of non-veterans regardless of their scores. For promotional positions, disabled veterans and veterans have preference over non-veterans when a disabled veteran or veteran is at the top of a certification of the list to an appointing authority.

findings.name: New Jersey Veterans Memorial Homes
findings.description: New Jersey's Division of Veterans Healthcare Services operates three long-term care nursing homes for veterans, in Paramus (the state's oldest, opened 1899, rebuilt 2005, 300 residents), Menlo Park (rebuilt 1999, 312 beds), and Vineland (Medicare-certified and VA-certified). All three are inspected and licensed annually by the NJ Department of Health and the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, and are open to veterans honorably discharged from war or peacetime service, their spouses, and Gold Star parents/spouses of service members killed in action during a period of war.
findings.value: Long-term nursing home care at three state veterans memorial homes
otherReqs: Honorable discharge from war or peacetime service
Spouses and Gold Star parents/spouses also eligible
findings.agency: New Jersey Department of Military and Veterans Affairs, Division of Veterans Healthcare Services
documentation: DD-214 or other proof of military service
findings.sourceExcerpt: The Division of Veterans Healthcare Services operates three modern long-term care nursing homes located in Paramus, Menlo Park, and Vineland. The facilities are open to veterans who were honorably discharged from U.S. war or peacetime services, the veteran's spouse, and to spouses and parents of members of the military who were killed in action during a period of war (Gold Star Parent).
